subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB459.md LANDED. FORMAT 14 GR29 - 'If arithmetic-expression-4 does not evaluate to a nonnegative integer, the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist and the execution of the SET statement is unsuccessful' (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). Both consequents now happen, for all three of GR30's forms, because the test is on the AMOUNT and GR30 a/b/c compute the new capacity from it afterwards. EmitSetCapacity lands the amount through the same CobolIndex.TryAmount the two index formats use, with SetAmountRule.Capacity adding GR29's own sign test; the table call sits inside the success leg, so an unsuccessful SET computes no new capacity at all. GR30's minimum-capacity clamp deliberately still stands and is NOT the implementation of GR29 - the clamp is the rule for a legal new capacity below the OCCURS minimum, and GR29 rejects the operand before any new capacity exists. MEASURED before, at --std 2014 with checking ON: 'SET CAP TO 5' then 'SET CAP TO A' (A PIC S9(4) VALUE -3) printed CAP2=0 - the negative was carried in and clamped to the minimum, DESTROYING five live occurrences - and 'SET CAP TO B' (B PIC 9V9 VALUE 3.5) printed CAP3=3, truncating and shrinking. MEASURED after: SUB=EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT for each, CAP2=0000000005 and CAP3=0000000005, and the control 'SET CAP DOWN BY 2' still reaches GR30 c) and gives CAP4=0000000003. A sibling narrowing one frame below was repaired in the same change (CobolDynTable now computes the new capacity in Int128 and tests it against the implementor maximum BEFORE narrowing - a request of 5000000000 used to WRAP through an (int) cast into a small valid capacity instead of raising GR30's EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT).
